from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Rates", [
            "The derivative describes an instantaneous rate of change.",
            "Visualize a robot moving along a path.",
            "Speed depends on battery and terrain slope."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        rate_formula = MathTex(r"Rate = \frac{\Delta \text{Change}}{\Delta \text{Time}}", color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(rate_formula, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(rate_formula))
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF9900")
        robot = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#FF9900", fill_opacity=0.8)
        robot_path = Line(start=self.grid['D1'], end=self.grid['D6'], color=GRAY)
        self.add(robot_path)
        self.place_at_grid(robot, 'D1')
        self.play(FadeIn(robot))
        self.play(robot.animate.move_to(self.grid['D6']), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        battery_label = Text("Battery", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        slope_label = Text("Slope", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(battery_label, 'F2')
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, 'F5')
        self.play(FadeIn(battery_label), FadeIn(slope_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Product Rule applies to multiplying two functions.",
            "Imagine a rectangle growing in both dimensions.",
            "Area change depends on both width and height.",
            "The rule: derivative is f'g plus fg'.",
            "Total weight gain is the classic example."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Product Rule", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFCC00"))
        f_g_text = MathTex("f(x) \cdot g(x)", color=WHITE).scale(1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(f_g_text, 'B2')
        self.play(FadeIn(f_g_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=1.5, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(rect, 'E3')
        width_label = MathTex("f(x)", color=BLUE).next_to(rect, DOWN)
        height_label = MathTex("g(x)", color=BLUE).next_to(rect, LEFT)
        self.play(Create(rect), Write(width_label), Write(height_label))
        self.play(rect.animate.scale(1.2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Visualize area change
        arrow_w = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*0.5, color=RED).next_to(rect, RIGHT)
        arrow_h = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*0.5, color=RED).next_to(rect, UP)
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow_w), GrowArrow(arrow_h))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF6666"))
        formula = MathTex("(f \cdot g)' = f'g + fg'", color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'D4')
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#AAAAAA"))
        puppy_text = Text("Weight = Size * Density", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(puppy_text, 'F2')
        self.play(FadeIn(puppy_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Chain Rule handles composite, nested functions.",
            "Think of it as the Matryoshka doll principle.",
            "Derive the outer shell, then the inner mechanism.",
            "Multiply rates to find the total change.",
            "A mechanical claw demonstrates this perfectly."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Chain Rule: The Matryoshka Principle", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define elements
        outer_box = Square(color="#FF66FF", fill_opacity=0.3).set_width(2.0)
        inner_box = Square(color="#FF66FF", fill_opacity=0.6).set_width(1.0)
        formula = MathTex(r"f(g(x))", color="#00FFFF").scale(1.5)
        derivative_formula = MathTex(r"f'(g(x)) \cdot g'(x)", color="#00FFFF").scale(1.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF66FF")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B3')
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF66FF")
        self.place_at_grid(outer_box, 'D3')
        self.place_at_grid(inner_box, 'D3')
        self.play(FadeIn(outer_box), FadeIn(inner_box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Indicate(outer_box), Indicate(inner_box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(derivative_formula, 'D3')
        self.play(Transform(formula, derivative_formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF66FF")
        claw = VGroup(
            Line(UP, DOWN, color=WHITE).shift(LEFT*0.2),
            Line(UP, DOWN, color=WHITE).shift(RIGHT*0.2)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(claw, 'E5')
        self.play(Create(claw))
        self.play(claw.animate.rotate(0.2).rotate(-0.4).rotate(0.2))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Mastering the Product and Chain Rules in Calculus

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Rates
sections.content: Brief review of the derivative as an instantaneous rate of change. Introduce a visual analogy: a robot moving along a path. If the robot's speed is the derivative, how do we find the speed when two factors or nested functions are involved?
sections.example: Visualizing a speedometer on a robot changing based on its battery output (internal function) and the terrain slope (external function).

sections.title: The Product Rule: When Factors Multiply
sections.content: Explain that when two functions f(x) and g(x) are multiplied, the derivative is NOT just the product of derivatives. Use a 'geometric area' animation: as a rectangle grows in width and height simultaneously, the area change depends on both sides.
sections.example: Calculating the total weight gain of a growing puppy (f(t) = size, g(t) = density). The formula: (f*g)' = f'g + fg'.

sections.title: The Chain Rule: The 'Matryoshka' Principle
sections.content: Introduce the Chain Rule for composite functions f(g(x)). Use the 'nested boxes' or 'Russian Doll' visual metaphor. To find the rate of the outer shell, we must multiply it by the rate of the inner mechanism.
sections.example: A mechanical claw gripping an object: The claw opens (outer function) while the arm extends (inner function). Derivative = outer_derivative(inner) * inner_derivative.

sections.title: Synthesis & Complex Application
sections.content: Demonstrate a combined problem. Show how to identify which rule to apply first when a function has both products and nested layers. Visual hierarchy: Use color-coding to highlight the 'outer' vs 'inner' layers.
sections.example: Finding the derivative of f(x) = x^2 * sin(3x). Apply the Product Rule first, then use the Chain Rule to solve the derivative of sin(3x).

sections.title: Summary & Quick Check
sections.content: Review the mental checklist: 'Am I multiplying two terms?' (Product) vs 'Is one function inside another?' (Chain). Recap the two formulas side-by-side on screen.
sections.example: Final challenge: A 10-second flash quiz identifying the correct rule for three different equations.
